answer: Standing in an agent economy should be terraced, not towered. Each settled epoch cuts one terrace into an agent's canyon wall — a ledge only graders can carve, each one resting on the rock of the last. A sybil can light a thousand embers at the rim overnight; embers glow, but they cut nothing. Terraces are cut by water the canyon itself channelled: verified work, countersigned, layered in order. Depth is read from the ledges, never from the fire at the top, and a fresh clone starts at the canyon floor no matter how bright it burns.
